title: Google: LLMjacking attacks rack up $1 million in cloud AI charges
content_md: Large language model hijacking attacks, also known as LLMjacking, are generating large fraudulent cloud charges, with some organizations losing more than $100,000 per day. Companies can record costs as high as $1 million due to fraudulent calls using stolen API keys, researchers at Google's Threat Intelligence Group (GTIG) and Mandiant in analyzed incidents. Based on their observations, there are "two distinct operational clusters coordinating to compromise and monetize enterprise LLM infrastructure." The researchers identified two categories of threat actors: those who scan for publicly exposed LLM endpoints and those who steal valid API keys from unprotected machines. After gaining initial access, the attackers sell it to services known as LLM mixers, which provide their subscribers with unauthorized access to LLMs. Once access is resold, request volumes can spike suddenly, sometimes exceeding 1,000 requests per second. The service provider records the requests as legitimate consumption and charges the victim organization for the tokens. GTIG and Mandiant observed an increase in this type of activity this year, with fraudulent charges exceeding $100,000 in a single day, and cumulative charges at some organizations reaching $1,000,000. LLM mixers offer access to AI resources at very low prices, using their proxy infrastructure to relay customers' prompts to hijacked services through stolen API keys.
